title: Invoice Closure, Reopening and Statement Services (Patient Invoices & Statements)
content:
A Patient Invoices & Statements invoice whose balance reaches zero through payments is paid; one whose balance reaches zero through adjustments or a write-off is closed, the billing class's closing days after the balance reached zero. The invoice record shows the date the balance reached zero.

## Paid and closed

| How the balance reaches zero | Resulting status |
|---|---|
| Patient payments | Paid |
| Payments under a payment plan that pay the balance off | Paid |
| The collection agency collects the balance in full | Paid |
| Adjustments | Closed |
| A small-balance write-off | Closed |

## Reopening

A paid invoice becomes open again only when a payment that settled it is reversed. A consumer purchase, paid at purchase, is paid from the start and only reopens through a reversal.

## Itemized statements

An itemized statement is sent on request within the billing class's itemized-statement business days, at the class's itemized-statement fee.

## Paperless statements

Statements go by email instead of paper only to patients enrolled in the patient portal, and only where the billing class offers paperless statements.

| Patient enrolled in the patient portal | Class offers paperless statements | Statements by email |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | any | No |
| any | No | No |

## Illustrations (hypothetical invoices)

- An invoice of 95.00 is settled by a card payment of 95.00: it is paid. If that card payment is later charged back, the invoice is open again with 95.00 due.
- An invoice of 40.00 is brought to zero by a billing error correction: it is closed, not paid.
- A Consumer Test Purchase Invoice, paid at purchase, stays paid unless the purchase payment is reversed.
